hero.title: Generics
intro.0: You have used List<T> - a type that works with any kind of value. Now write your own. Four small programs you build from scratch and run: a Box<T>, a generic method, a Pair<A, B>, and a generic method that returns a generic type. Write the type, run it, match the output.
task.1.title: A box for anything
task.1.context: A generic type works with any kind of value. You write a placeholder - `T` - in angle brackets, and the caller picks the real type. You have used `List<T>` already; now write your own. Define a `Box<T>` that holds one value of whatever type `T` is.
task.1.goal.0: Define `public class Box<T>` with a `T Value` set through its constructor.
task.1.goal.1: Main makes a `Box<int>` holding 7 and prints `Value`, so the output is 7.
task.2.title: A method that works on any array
task.2.context: A method can be generic too: put the `<T>` after its name, and it works on any type. Write `First<T>` that takes an array of `T` and returns its first item. The caller's type is worked out automatically from the array passed in.
task.2.goal.0: Give `Picker` a method `public T First<T>(T[] items)` that returns `items[0]`.
task.2.goal.1: Main calls `First` on the int array `{ 3, 4, 5 }`, so the output is 3.
task.3.title: Two types at once
task.3.context: A type can take more than one placeholder. `Pair<A, B>` holds two values whose types can differ - like a name and an age. Separate the placeholders with a comma.
task.3.goal.0: Define `public class Pair<A, B>` with a `First` of type `A` and a `Second` of type `B`, both set in the constructor.
task.3.goal.1: Main makes a `Pair<string, int>` of "age" and 3 and prints `First + ": " + Second`, so the output is age: 3.
task.4.title: Put them together
task.4.concept: Generic method returning a generic type
task.4.context: Generic classes and generic methods combine. `Box<T>` is already written for you. Add a generic method `Wrap<T>` that takes a `T` and returns a `Box<T>` holding it - so the method's `T` flows straight into the type it builds.
task.4.goal.0: Give `Wrapper` a method `public Box<T> Wrap<T>(T item)` that returns `new Box<T>(item)`.
task.4.goal.1: Main wraps 5 and prints the box's `Value`, so the output is 5.
